name: ts-advisor
description: A recommending-ts-tooling skill: profiles the project's TypeScript toolchain offline (scripts, dependencies, the tsconfig chain, eslint/vitest/knip config, cap counts, verify-step wiring), then fans out live research over official upstream tooling sources before recommending what's missing -- tsconfig flags, module resolution, typed linting, testing, packaging validation, dependency hygiene, pnpm supply-chain settings, scripts and verify gates, monorepo/catalogs, Node pinning, and release automation. Every recommendation carries a source URL fetched in that run; a failed fetch is reported as unverified, never recommended anyway. Read-only: no hooks, no settings, no scripts, no gate -- pure file drop of one skill plus its reference material.
adoptNotes: Reuses templates/core's own typescript-guidance allowlist (references/typescript-sources.md) for the T1/T2 TypeScript-owner tier rather than duplicating it -- this pack's own references/tooling-sources.md only adds the sibling tier for pnpm/knip/vitest/eslint/prettier/npm/Node-release tooling that typescript-guidance's allowlist doesn't cover. requires.paths makes this a hard install error in FRESH mode if the required file is somehow missing -- it never is in practice, since typescript-guidance ships unconditionally as one of templates/core's own baseline skills. In ADOPT mode, /customize installs a pack's files by hand rather than through the CLI's own requires.paths check (see templates/packs/README.md's "Install path"), so an adopted project that never had templates/core's typescript-guidance skill (or removed it) can still receive this pack with the required file genuinely absent -- that is the one case the recommending-ts-tooling skill's own runtime fallback exists for: it still installs and runs, says the allowlist is missing plainly, and researches only against its own tooling-sources.md tier rather than falling back to an unlisted domain. This pack never touches an existing compiler flag or config value that already exists: recommending a change to something already configured is typescript-guidance's job (research or refresh mode), not this pack's -- see the skill's own "Authority split" section.
